A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HarmoniCa. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments, quality and latency measurements, training-cost comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and reports additional benchmark, baseline, ablation and sampler-transfer results.

M1.justification: V3's Change Logs explicitly state that cross-attention feature caching is added after being omitted in v1. This extends the components being cached; the SDT training procedure, IEPO objective and core router algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ImageNet and MS-COCO evaluations, v3 adds MJHQ-30K and sDCI experiments, extending quantitative evaluation to high-quality image and dense-caption distributions (Appendix J, Table 16). The underlying class-conditional and text-to-image tasks remain the same.

E2.justification: V3 adds U-ViT comparisons with Faster Diffusion and DeepCache (Table 4), and a standalone acceleration comparison including PTQ4DiT, Diff-Pruning and the previously evaluated EfficientDM (Table 5). FORA also joins the PIXART-alpha 512 qualitative comparison. Learning-to-Cache, FORA and Delta-DiT remain in their existing comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include U-ViT with 20-step DPM-Solver on A6000, A100 latency measurements, additional sampler/resolution configurations, and controlled router transfer between samplers. Appendix J specifies 30K MJHQ and 5K sDCI samples with ImageReward, LPIPS and PSNR. The retained main experiments still specify the same 20K training budget and 50K/30K evaluation sample counts.

E4.justification: V3 adds comparative quality-versus-speed curves (Figure 7), threshold sensitivity (Table 8), MS-SSIM and LPIPS proxy ablations (Table 7), sampler-transfer tests (Table 17), and qualitative baseline error comparisons (Figures 11–12). The original component, update-interval, regularization, optimization-deviation and sampling-strategy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions mention a fixed random seed for visualization examples but report no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises many PIXART results: for 20-step DPM-Solver++ at 256 resolution, HarmoniCa's reported FID changes from 27.61 to 26.33 and FORA's from 38.20 to 27.42. HarmoniCa now includes cross-attention caching, so these are revised-method results. Numerous baseline, benchmark and analysis entries are added. Table 2 remains unchanged, while Section 5.2 corrects its 10-step IS description from 206.57 to 151.83.

T1.justification: The cache, router and CUR definitions, losses, masking construction and image-error proxy equations are retained. V3 adds no substantive mathematical derivation, assumption, theorem or proof; the additional perceptual metrics are empirical ablation choices.

C1.justification: The central SDT/IEPO contributions and approximately 25% training-time reduction claim remain. The abstract and introduction expand the advertised model count from seven to eight and replace the first-method, over-1.5x PIXART-alpha example with claims of over 40% latency reduction and 2.07x theoretical speedup.

C2.justification: Appendix K newly recommends matching training and inference samplers, attributing transfer degradation to different trajectories and noise schedules. V3 also adds hardware and sampler explanations for quantization results, qualifies inference overhead, and explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to block-wise image generation.

D1.justification: V3 documents PTQ4DiT's DDIM adaptation, Diff-Pruning's DiT reimplementation, hardware for added comparisons and an additional PIXART-Sigma hyperparameter configuration. Conversely, it drops v1's general batch-size-eight statement for latency measurements. This omission does not establish an actual batch-size change.

R1.justification: V3 adds token-caching work by Zou et al. and Lou et al., clarifying its block-wise scope and exclusion of finer-grained comparators. It also adds references supporting U-ViT, PTQ4DiT, cross-attention, new datasets and perceptual metrics. The overall diffusion, compression and feature-caching positioning remains.

P1.justification: V3 compresses and rewrites the abstract and conclusion, standardizes caching terminology, moves the quantization-combination discussion into Section 5.2, and reorganizes appendix headings. It adds limitations, impact and change-log text, while retaining the overall six-section progression and most method exposition.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with substantially resized and rearranged tables and figures. V3 adds comparison displays and highlighted qualitative examples, replaces Figure 1, and reduces or replaces several T2I galleries. Core diagrams and several original ablation plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons, additional dataset evaluations and the sampler-transfer failure analysis strengthen empirical support and practical guidance. V3 also corrects the 10-step IS description to match Table 2. These improve an already substantial evaluation, although cross-attention implementation remains briefly described and the general latency batch-size disclosure is lost, limiting the reproducibility gains.
